text:
alex_cs: FYI — PeerPair onboarding noticed a sudden spike of 429s after we enabled the browser SDK in their staging site. They ramped from ~10 concurrent users to a short burst ~400 parallel requests.
ben_customer: seeing `429` with `Retry-After: 5` on almost every request for ~30s. No 401s, auth looks good. Using our browser SDK v0.8.1 + service worker caching.
alex_cs: first guess is preflight/fanout from ephemeral token refresh + many tabs. They use short-lived tokens renewed per tab. Also header shows `x-rw-route: sdkgateway-eu`.
carol_platform: can you drop a small httplog snippet? Also which transport — HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2? HTTP/2 multiplexing behavior changes how pools saturate.
ben_customer: paste of browser console snippet:
```
POST https://api.redwood.io/v1/generate 429
retry-after: 5
x-rate-limit-reset: 1719987745
content-length: 0
```
No obvious 401s. Client is doing 50 parallel fetches from one tab.
alex_cs: thanks. Quick checklist: 1) are they using `preflight: true` (browser SDK preflight to check tokens)? 2) do they pin region? 3) alignment of `keepalive`/connection reuse in fetch calls.
ben_customer: they're not using preflight explicitly — default browser SDK flow. They are doing `client.generate` per message and not batching. Many requests originate from a worker that opens a new connection per call.
carol_platform: a likely vector: connection pool exhaustion at our edge/proxy when many short-lived TLS handshakes + no keepalive. Browser fetch with `keepalive` disabled + service worker scope per-tab can cause bursts. TL;DR: server returns 429 when ephemeral token validation + routing queues hit capacity.
alex_cs: suggested mitigations to try:
- enable client-side batching where possible (group user messages)
- ensure SDK reuses a single shared client instance across tabs/workers
- set `maxConcurrency` in SDK to 8-12
- enable preflight coalescing or add small jitter on retry
- for long-running background tasks use a stable token renewal endpoint (not per-request)
ben_customer: can we see any server-side logs to verify connection closure rate? Also is there a per-IP throttle that might affect them behind NAT?
carol_platform: checking logs now — seeing a ~350 reqs/s spike from a single IP with >80% short-lived TLS session time < 200ms and `CONNECT` churn. Proxy has a soft per-route concurrent request cap that starts queueing and emits 429 when queue > 50 for >10s. It's not per-customer token, it's route-level protective behavior.
dave_oncall: looping in oncall. If customer tries mitigation and still gets 429s we'll consider temporary burst allowance for that route while they onboard.
alex_cs: immediate action plan I sent to customer:
1) reduce concurrency in SDK (set env var or patch quick build)
2) enable sharing client instance across pages/workers
3) add exponential backoff with jitter and respect Retry-After
4) send a small sample of requests after these changes and we’ll tail logs
ben_customer: applying concurrency cap now (8) and switching to single client instance. Will report back in ~10m.
deploy-bot: Deploy 0.8.2 of browser-sdk to staging queued — will contain `maxConcurrency` opt.
ben_customer: quick update — after lowering concurrency to 8 the 429s dropped to a few sporadic ones and latency improved. Thanks!
alex_cs: great — we'll keep monitoring, and if you hit any persistent spikes we can schedule a small one-time capacity bump. Also noted as onboarding learn: recommend SDK default maxConcurrency be conservative for first-run.
carol_platform: filed internal ticket #CS-6482 to add clearer doc snippets about single-client usage and service-worker patterns. Assigning to devex.
ben_customer: appreciate the help all :thumbsup:
alex_cs: thank you — marking this thread resolved unless something else pops up.
